description: Sector overlay for U.S. technology companies, SaaS, software, cloud, AI, cybersecurity, privacy, consumer-data, platform, and software-supply-chain documentation.

metadata.scope: United States sector overlay controls for Technology. Intended to be used with us/core_control_library.
metadata.source_note: Source basis revalidated against authoritative U.S. federal statutes, regulations, agency and regulator materials, and applicable model/professional or industry standards available through 2026-08-30. This rule pack remains an evidence-screening control set, not legal advice, and requires qualified legal/compliance review before production reliance. State, territorial, tribal, and local requirements may impose additional obligations.
metadata.external_knowledge_policy: No external knowledge is introduced during document evaluation. Regulatory source mappings live only in this versioned rule pack.

rules.title: Consumer privacy notice, data-use, or consent evidence is present
rules.summary: Checks for privacy notice, personal information, data use, consent, opt-out, deletion, or consumer rights evidence.

rules.title: Cybersecurity risk management and incident-response evidence is documented
rules.summary: Checks for cybersecurity risk-management, access control, vulnerability management, incident response, and breach-notification evidence, using NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 as the current voluntary framework reference where appropriate.

rules.title: Secure software development or software-supply-chain controls are documented
rules.summary: Checks for secure software-development and software-supply-chain controls aligned where appropriate to NIST SP 800-218 SSDF v1.1, including SBOM/component governance, vulnerability disclosure, provenance/third-party controls, and secure development practices. NIST SP 800-218 Rev. 1 / SSDF v1.2 remains draft and is not treated as the current final baseline.

rules.title: Child-data controls are present where children-directed services are referenced
rules.summary: Checks for child-data controls under the 2025 amended COPPA Rule, including verifiable parental consent, separate consent for targeted advertising/other third-party disclosures where required, data-retention limits, and expanded personal-information categories such as biometric identifiers.
